title: The Delivery
epigraph: A courier, a sealed pouch, and a name he recognised.
blurb: A sealed pouch with black wax, a destination he should have read first, and a name on the manifest that a courier in Haven City does not want to recognise.

image.depicts: A narrow wet street in Haven City at night, Bone Patrol checkpoint lights turning the rain silver two blocks north. No figures.
image.spoilerCheck: PASS. Shows only weather and geography. No courier, no pouch, no Sev'oran.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-4 FESTIVAL NEON, seen through rain, at street level.

>>> REGISTER: THIS IS NOT THE PROLOGUES. <<<
No Tower, no plaza, no gate, no monument, nothing enormous. This is an ordinary
narrow working street in Haven City on a wet night, the kind of street people
live above and buy dinner on. Keep the camera low and human and let the
buildings be close on both sides. The picture should feel like somewhere you
could walk, not somewhere you would be summoned to.

>>> NO LOCATION REFERENCE IS ATTACHED, DELIBERATELY. <<<
This street has not been drawn before and it is not the alley from a later
plate in this Tale. Build it from the description here.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: WET NEON, DOUBLED IN THE ROAD, AND ONE COLD WHITE END. <<<
The street surface is soaked and it reflects everything: MAGENTA, CYAN, AMBER
and hot pink running down it in long broken streaks. Warm light spills from
ground-floor windows and doorways. Rain is visibly falling and every light in
the frame has a halo on it.
TWO BLOCKS NORTH, at the far end, a BONE PATROL CHECKPOINT is running and its
light is different from everything else in the picture: COLD, WHITE, HARD, and
it turns the falling rain SILVER at that end of the frame. It is small with
distance and it is the only cold thing here. The whole composition is the
distance between the warm crowded near end and that cold white far end.

NO FIGURES ANYWHERE IN THIS PLATE. Nobody in the street, nobody in a doorway,
no silhouette at the checkpoint. The street is occupied and everyone is inside
out of the rain, and the evidence of them is what fills the picture:
  - lit windows above the shopfronts, curtains, plants on sills, the shapes of
    rooms
  - a vendor stall shuttered for the night under a dripping awning
  - laundry lines strung between the buildings, forgotten in the rain
  - stacked crates, bicycles chained to railings, a cat's-eye of light under a
    door
This is a lived-in street with an occupied evening happening above it.

CAMERA: LOW, STREET LEVEL, LOOKING NORTH ALONG THE ROAD, so the wet surface
carries the reflections the full width of the picture and the checkpoint sits
small and cold at the vanishing point.

2:1 LANDSCAPE. Compose so the LEFT half and the RIGHT half each work alone and
keep the centre strip free of anything load-bearing — the fold runs through it.
The road can run through the middle; the checkpoint should sit off centre.

title.title: The Delivery
title.epigraph: A courier, a sealed pouch, and a name he recognised.

blocks.v: The Absalom Job

The dispatch work dried up in the rainy season, so when a sealed pouch with black wax landed on his table at the Courier's Exchange, Pixels took the job before he read the destination. That was the first mistake, and he knew it while he was making it, which didn't stop him.

He tilted the pouch toward the window light. The skull in the wax was pressed deep, the kind of stamp that required weight behind it. Absalom's sigil. He had run adjacently to Bone Patrol work for three years, carrying supply manifests and shift schedules, the kind of paper that kept the machine moving without touching the machine itself. He had told himself that was a distinction that mattered.
The handler in the doorway was watching him.
"Third Patrol Station," she said. "Sector Four. Shift commander, not the desk. You hand it to the commander or you bring it back."
"I know how delivery works," Pixels said.
"First time running direct for a Lord, your face goes somewhere. Wanted to make sure yours wasn't going there."
He put the pouch in his bag. His face displayed a pale blue grid pattern that he used when he wanted it to display nothing. "I'm fine," he said.
She let him go. The street outside was narrow and wet and the Bone Patrol's white checkpoint lights turned the rain silver two blocks north. He walked south.

image.caption: The skull in the wax was pressed deep. The kind of stamp that required weight behind it.
image.depicts: A sealed pouch on a table at the Courier's Exchange, tilted toward window light, Absalom's skull sigil pressed into black wax.
image.hardConstraints: The wax seal is the subject and must be sharp and central. Pixels' hands may be in frame; his face is not. Seal UNBROKEN.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-3 SKYLINE DAY, indoors, hard directional daylight.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: WARM PAPER AND CREAM, AND ONE PIECE OF ABSOLUTE BLACK. <<<
The plate before this is a wet neon night. This one is dry, bright and warm —
daylight through a tall window, cream stone, worn wood, brown paper, brass. It
should feel like an ordinary morning at work.
THE BLACK WAX SEAL IS THE ONLY TRUE BLACK IN THE PICTURE and it is the whole
point: a hard, deep, light-swallowing disc in the middle of a warm bright room.

{{LOC:COURIERS_EXCHANGE}}

>>> SHOT SCALE: CLOSE OBJECT STUDY. A TABLETOP, NOT A ROOM. <<<
CAMERA: LOW AND CLOSE OVER THE TABLE, almost at its surface, angled so the hard
window light rakes across the pouch and throws a long shadow off it. The room
is present only as warm out-of-focus depth behind — pigeonhole racks, hanging
task boards, stacked pouches — never sharp, never the subject.

>>> THE SUBJECT IS A SEAL. <<<
A leather-and-canvas courier POUCH lies on a worn sorting table, tilted toward
the window. Set into its flap is a disc of BLACK WAX with a SKULL SIGIL pressed
deep into it — deep enough that a viewer can see it took weight to make. Sharp,
central, and the most detailed thing in the frame.
THE SEAL IS UNBROKEN. Whole, uncracked, undisturbed. It gets broken two plates
from now and that must still be ahead of us.

{{CHAR:PIXELS}}
>>> WE MUST SEE HIS FACE. A PREVIOUS VERSION SHOWED ONLY HIS HANDS AND IT COST
>>> THE PLATE ITS CHARACTER. <<<
Pixels is LEANING IN OVER THE TABLE from the far side, head and shoulders in
frame, looking down at the seal. Shoot him from the front or three-quarter so
the display is fully visible — never from behind, never cropped at the neck.
HIS DISPLAY SHOWS THE PALE BLUE GRID, calm and even, throwing a faint cool
light down onto the pouch that sits against all the warm daylight in the room.
His hands are on the pouch, one steadying it and one tilting it into the light,
segmented fingers, working-worn, unhurried.

THE SEAL IS STILL THE SUBJECT. He is above and behind it, slightly soft, and it
is the sharpest thing in the frame — but a reader should be able to see exactly
who is looking at it and that he has gone still.

BACKGROUND LIFE, SOFT AND UNREADABLE BUT PRESENT: two or three other couriers
further down the room going through their own work — sorting, stamping, hefting
a bag onto a shoulder. This is a busy working dispatch room on an ordinary day
and the story has not started yet for anyone but him.

NO READABLE CHARACTERS ANYWHERE. The task boards, labels, tags and manifests all
carry the rhythm of writing with no formed word in them.

blocks.v: What The Message Said

He broke the seal in the alley behind the water reclamation building. He had done this three times in his career, read things he was paid not to read, and each time he had resealed the envelope and delivered it anyway, because the information was never about him and the job was the job. He told himself he was checking the address. He had broken the seal before he finished the thought.

The paper was Bone Patrol formatted. He knew their column layouts: terse, numbered, written to be acted on rather than argued with. Date at the top. Authorization codes he didn't recognize in the margin. A name, centered, in larger type than anything else on the page.
Sev'oran. Residential Block 14, Third Floor.

His floor. The Valari woman three doors down who kept dried protein strips on the hallway radiator and had explained, when he'd mentioned the smell, that they discouraged rats. She'd laughed when she said it. He hadn't understood why until the second week, when he noticed she was right. He had knocked on her door after that and she'd been surprised, not by the knock but by what he said, which was thank you, and she'd looked at him the way people looked at Synthetics when Synthetics said things that weren't technically necessary.
Below her name, the order used the word detention. Compound Seven. There was no release column on the form.

image.caption: A name, centered, in larger type than anything else on the page.
image.depicts: Pixels in an alley behind the water reclamation building, the broken seal hanging, the order held in the rain. Sev'oran's name legible on the page.
image.hardConstraints: Pixels is a Synthetic — his face is a display surface, currently a pale blue grid. The seal is BROKEN in this image. Rain visibly falling.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-1 NIGHT NOIR, cold and wet.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: COLD RAIN, ONE SILVER FAR END, AND HIS FACE AS A LIGHT. <<<
The plate before this is warm dry daylight; this is the cold outside of it.
Deep blue-green dark, wet pipework, black standing water, rain falling hard
enough to see. Two blocks north the alley opens onto the checkpoint and its
COLD WHITE light turns the rain SILVER at that end.
THE SECOND LIGHT SOURCE IN THIS PICTURE IS HIS FACE. Pixels' display is a PALE
BLUE GRID and it throws real blue light onto the paper he is holding, onto the
rain in front of him, and onto the wet wall beside him. It is the only warm-side
colour in a cold plate and it is close to camera, so it does the lighting work
that a lamp would normally do.

{{LOC:RECLAMATION_ALLEY}}

>>> SHOT SCALE: CLOSE, OVER HIS SHOULDER, ONTO THE PAGE. <<<
CAMERA: TIGHT AND BEHIND HIM at head height, over one shoulder, so we read the
page he is reading and see the alley only as depth past it. The opener is the
wide street; this one is a page in the rain and two walls. Do not shoot it wide.

{{CHAR:PIXELS}}
ONE FIGURE. Pixels, standing still in the rain, seen from behind and slightly to
one side. Hood up, shoulders wet through, water running off him. He has stopped
moving completely.

>>> THE SEAL IS BROKEN IN THIS PLATE. <<< The pouch hangs open in his other hand
with the black wax split and its two halves still attached — clearly opened,
clearly not resealed yet.

THE ORDER IS HELD OUT IN THE RAIN AND IT IS GETTING WET. Bone Patrol paper:
terse, numbered, a rigid column layout, a date block at the top and code
markings in the margin. One NAME sits centred in the middle of the page in type
noticeably larger than everything around it.
NOT ONE READABLE CHARACTER ANYWHERE ON IT. The name must read as A NAME — the
eye must land on it and know that is what it is — purely from its size, its
placement and the space around it, without a single formed letter. Rain is
beginning to bleed the marks.

Nobody else in the alley. No Bone Patrol figure in frame; the checkpoint is only
light at a distance.

blocks.v: He stood in the alley for longer than was professional. The rain found the gaps in his hoodie and he didn't move. He was thinking about what the word detention meant in this city, in a Bone Patrol document, for a Valari who had done nothing he'd ever seen except keep the rats out of the hallway. He was thinking about the three times he'd read something and delivered it anyway.
He resealed the pouch. His hands were steady in the mechanical way they got when he stopped asking them questions.

He walked to the station. He delivered the pouch to the shift commander and watched the commander break the seal and start reading. He walked out through the patrol bay with the careful pace of someone who had nothing to be careful about. Two officers by the door tracked him with their red optics. He kept his visor neutral, no color, no pattern, just dark glass in a pale frame, and he didn't look back until he was far enough away that not looking back was no longer information.
Then he ran.
Third Floor

The stairs in his building were narrow and his neighbors had learned not to leave things in the stairwell, but tonight someone had left a child's jacket on the second-floor landing and he stepped around it and kept moving.

image.caption: He walked out through the patrol bay with the careful pace of someone who had nothing to be careful about.
image.depicts: Pixels crossing the Third Patrol Station bay toward the exit, two Bone Patrol officers by the door tracking him with red optics. His visor is blank dark glass.
image.hardConstraints: Visor shows NO colour and NO pattern — just dark glass in a pale frame. He is not hurrying. The officers are watching, not moving.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-1 NIGHT NOIR, institutional, with one working overhead.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: COLD INSTITUTIONAL GREY-GREEN AND SMALL RED POINTS. <<<
Poured floor, painted lane and chevron markings, structural ribs, equipment
racks. Drained of warmth: grey-green, gunmetal, pale concrete. The only
saturated colour is RED — small indicator points on the equipment racks, and
the ORANGE-RED optics of the two officers at the far door.
THE BAY IS DARK BY DESIGN, SO GIVE IT ONE WORKING OVERHEAD FIXTURE NEAR THE
MIDDLE that puts light on the floor and on the crossing figure. He must not
become a silhouette in a black room; we need to see that he is calm.

{{LOC:PATROL_STATION}}

>>> SHOT SCALE: MEDIUM WIDE, THE BAY RECEDING TO THE DOOR. <<<
CAMERA: EYE LEVEL, AHEAD OF HIM AND OFF TO ONE SIDE, near the exit doorway,
LOOKING BACK UP THE BAY AS HE WALKS TOWARD US.
>>> WE SEE HIS FACE, NOT THE BACK OF HIS HEAD. <<< An earlier version put the
camera behind him and the plate lost its character entirely — a hooded figure
from behind could be anyone. Turn it around. He walks toward camera; the length
of the bay, the racks and the parked vehicle recede behind him.
The two officers at the door piers are therefore NEAR CAMERA, one at each side
of frame, large and partly cut by the edges, with the bay and Pixels framed
between them. We are looking at him from where they are standing.
{{CHAR:PIXELS}}
>>> HIS VISOR IS BLANK DARK GLASS IN A PALE FRAME. NO COLOUR, NO GRID, NO
>>> PATTERN, NO LIGHT AT ALL. <<< In the plate before this it was a glowing blue
grid. Here it is switched off and shows nothing, and the difference between the
two is the entire performance he is giving. If anything is displayed on his
face, the plate has failed.

HE IS WALKING AT AN ORDINARY PACE. Not hurrying, not creeping, not glancing
back, not tense in the shoulders. His bag hangs empty and flat. This is a man
doing an unremarkable thing unremarkably, and the effort that takes is invisible.

{{CHAR:BONE_PATROL}}
TWO OFFICERS ONLY, ONE AT EACH PIER FLANKING THE FAR DOORWAY, exactly where they
stand. They are TRACKING HIM WITH THEIR OPTICS — heads turned, red-orange
sockets on him — and they are NOT MOVING. Not stepping out, not raising a hand,
not reaching for the hammer, not speaking. Watching is all they are doing and it
is enough.

BACKGROUND LIFE: further back in the bay, ordinary station business continues —
a parked patrol vehicle, an officer at the processing counter working through
paperwork, equipment being racked. This is a workplace on a normal shift, which
is what makes it frightening.

NO READABLE CHARACTERS ANYWHERE, including on the floor markings and the racks.

blocks.v: He had no plan. He understood that clearly. He was a courier with an empty bag and a broken employment relationship and a single piece of information that was worth something for a window of time that was already closing. He could hear, or imagined he could hear, the checkpoint lights humming two blocks north. He had given them a head start he couldn't calculate.
He stopped in front of her door. The smell of protein strips was faint now, either the batch was old or he was too focused to register it properly. He knocked.
Footsteps inside. The chain lock sliding free. The door opened and Sev'oran looked at him the way she always had, recognizing him, mildly curious, no reason yet to be anything else.
Pixels said: "Run."

image.caption: "Run."
image.depicts: Sev'oran's door open on the chain-freed latch, she and Pixels facing each other across the threshold. She is mildly curious, no reason yet to be anything else.
image.hardConstraints: Sev'oran's expression is NOT yet fear — recognition and mild curiosity only. Pixels' visor is blank. The hallway radiator with protein strips is visible behind him.
image.prompt:
{{STYLE}}
PALETTE MODE: PS-2 SUNSET EMBER, read as a warm dim hallway at night.

>>> COLOUR IDENTITY: THE WARMEST PLATE IN EITHER TALE, AND IT ENDS THE STORY. <<<
Everything before this has been wet neon, cold rain and a grey institutional
bay. This is somewhere people live. OCHRE AND AMBER from a single caged hallway
fixture, warm on worn panelling and a scuffed floor, deep soft shadow at the
edges. It should feel close, tired, small and cared for.
Through the open door behind her, a little more warm light from her rooms.
NOT sinister, NOT threatening, NOT cold. The words being said are frightening;
the room is not, and that gap is the picture.

{{LOC:RESIDENTIAL_BLOCK_14}}

>>> SHOT SCALE: TIGHT TWO-SHOT ACROSS A THRESHOLD. <<<
CAMERA: EYE LEVEL, CLOSE, FROM THE SIDE, so we get both faces and the door frame
between them, with the hallway falling away out of focus. The previous plate is
a wide cold bay; this one is two people and a doorway and almost nothing else.

{{CHAR:SEVORAN}}
{{CHAR:PIXELS}}
EXACTLY TWO FIGURES. Nobody else in the hallway, nobody on the stairs, no Bone
Patrol, no neighbour in a doorway.

SEV'ORAN stands in her own open doorway, the security chain hanging free where
she has just unhooked it, one hand still on the door edge. Practical indoor
clothes, worn soft. She is at home in the evening.

>>> HER EXPRESSION IS NOT FEAR AND MUST NOT BE. <<< It is RECOGNITION and MILD
CURIOSITY — the face you make for a neighbour you know, who has knocked at an
odd hour, before you have any reason to think anything is wrong. Slightly tired
around the eyes. Not alarmed, not braced, not backing away, not wide-eyed. She
has not heard the word yet. If she looks frightened the plate has failed,
because the whole moment is that she does not know.

PIXELS faces her across the threshold, rain still on his shoulders and dripping.
HIS VISOR IS BLANK DARK GLASS — no grid, no colour, no pattern — because he has
nothing he is willing to show. He gives the picture no expression at all, so
hers has to carry it.

THE HALLWAY BEHIND HIM MUST BE VISIBLY LIVED IN, and this is worth composing for:
the wall-mounted RADIATOR with DRIED PROTEIN STRIPS laid across it to cure, other
apartment doors with their own heavy latches and chains, a mat, a coat hook, a
child's small jacket left on the stair rail below. People live along this
corridor and are home tonight.

NO READABLE CHARACTERS ANYWHERE — no door numbers, no notices, no labels.
